evaluator: Independent advisory evaluator using a fictionalized Warren Sack analytical lens; Warren Sack did not participate, review, endorse, quote, or make a hiring decision.
evidence: The About page gives a rushed reader an explicit recurring sequence: observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, learn through use, and document enough for others to continue.

Harry J. Epstein Company is accurately delimited to 2009–2015 and visibly supplies every stage: customer and team relationships; an integrated commerce/operations model; incremental storefront releases; real customer and staff use; analytics- and question-led revision; and reusable patterns, ownership, and next-action handoff.

NYC Artist Coalition and FairRentNYC is marked CURRENT and supplies every stage: relationships among lived experience, meetings, sources, questions, and public actors; a recoverable civic-record model; campaign-page, meeting-format, and action-pathway increments; collective use in town halls, hearings, sessions, and campaigns; revision from meetings and public response; and handoff through minutes, source maps, question logs, and action trackers.

Sunday Dinner and 196 is marked CURRENT and supplies every stage: relationships grounded in hospitality, trust, support, space, and recurrence; a unified participation-system model; incremental invitation, onboarding, hosting, and access experiments; repeated participant and resident-artist use; revision through responses and practice; and continuity and residency-handoff patterns.

Structural-equivalence inflation is directly resisted: the three projects are said not to be equivalent in scale, maturity, authority, adoption, risk, or outcome. Production inflation is also resisted through historical dates, archived and unofficial labels, and the statement that source-backed team memory is an early working method rather than a completed client pilot or production SaaS.

Sole-authorship inflation is visibly resisted through co-built, co-led, contributed-to, collaborator, community-labor, and collective-outcome language. The FairRentNYC case explicitly says the work does not turn coalition campaigns or policy outcomes into one person's accomplishment.
The resume labels its web stack as current and historical experience and expressly states that historical implementation does not by itself establish present proficiency.

The rendered homepage photograph is presented with place, date, photographer credit, and archive context on desktop and mobile. Coalition and gathering captions likewise preserve project context and collective credit instead of implying depicted-person endorsement.

Participant privacy is operationalized rather than merely asserted: the Sunday Dinner/196 material withholds names, contacts, attendance histories, correspondence, access details, proposals, and unapproved images while exposing only aggregate evidence and redacted workflow structure.
safety_findings: The clearance note was applied only to the exact photo occurrences in this rendered candidate. It does not establish broader reuse permission, depicted-person endorsement, approval of another commit, or authority to index or publish elsewhere.
Photograph permission, credit, contextual integrity, dignity review, collective credit, and publication authority remain separate human responsibilities in the public text.
The candidate explicitly keeps private participant records and sensitive coalition context outside the public site and identifies unresolved consent or approval requirements.
The colophon explicitly states that fictionalized page-owner simulations are not participation, quotation, endorsement, approval, or sign-off and cannot grant consent or publication authority.
recommendation: Pass at score 4. The candidate makes the complete six-stage systems loop reconstructable across three clearly bounded projects while visibly preserving scope, credit, historical-proficiency, privacy, photographic-care, and endorsement boundaries.
